title: Measure: where does the gcd work happen?

questions.prompt: A fraction is built and its parts are never read (0 reads). Which package calls gcd fewer times?

choices.why: eager reduces when the fraction is built, so it has already made one call that nobody used.
lazy does its work only when a part is read. With no reads it makes no calls; eager has made one.
lazy postpones the work until a part is read, and no part is read.

checklist.step: Count the gcd calls a strategy really makes

hints: A strategy can only use the gcd function it is handed, so what you hand it decides what you can observe.
Module 1 counted calls the same way: a stand-in function that makes a note and then does the real work.
Inside measure define a function of (a, b) that adds one to a counter and returns gcd(a, b). Pass it as the strategy's last argument and return the strategy's result with the counter.
